To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
long-term simulated microgravity affects endothelial cells in terms of spheroid formation and protein expression.
long-term simulated microgravity induces formation of spheroids and tubular structures in endothelial cells.
long-term exposure to simulated microgravity induces endothelial dysfunction, angiogenesis and spheroid formation in ECs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of micro-gravity on ECs.
the influence of microenvironmental factors, such as gravity, on endothelial cells and may contribute to the understanding of the pathogenesis of cardiovascular complications in astronauts.
the influence of simulated microgravity on endothelial cell growth pattern and protein synthesis, and the possible role of proteins involved in angiogenesis, endothelial dysfunction and inflammation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a prolonged exposure to simulated microgravity induces a complex network of protein interactions in EA.hy926 cells, which may be relevant for cardiovascular complications in astronauts after a prolonged spaceflight.
the formation of MCS is a complex process that is influenced by the synthesis, release and degradation of a number of proteins.
a prolonged RPM exposure of ECs leads to an increase of proteins involved in cell structure, cell adhesion and angiogenesis, which might be associated with endothelial dysfunction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a 35-day simulated microgravity induces the formation of TS and MCS, which is accompanied by a complex modulation of gene expression and synthesis of several proteins involved in angiogenesis and vascular dysfunction.
the formation of MCS and TS in RPM-exposed ECs is accompanied by a change in protein expression, which might be associated with endothelial dysfunction and a proinflammatory status.
a long-term exposure to microgravity induces a network of interactions between proteins and cells that are involved in endothelial dysfunction and angiogenesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the formation of MCS and the release of pro-inflammatory and proangiogenic proteins might contribute to the development of cardiovascular complications in space.
the formation of MCS and tubules in ECs after a long-term exposure to simulated microgravity is a complex process involving several key proteins.
a prolonged exposure to simulated microgravity leads to changes in the expression and synthesis of proteins associated with cell structure and angiogenesis.
